title: Personal Credit Cards: Annual Fee Billing and Refund on Closure
content:
Personal Credit Cards tiers that carry an annual fee bill it once in each account year. This page states when the fee is billed, when it is not, and when it is given back because the card is closed.

## Billing

- The tier's annual fee is booked as an annual fee on the statement closing in the account's anniversary month, the anniversary month being the calendar month of the account's opening date.
- On a tier that forgoes the fee in the first account year, the earliest anniversary-month statement following the opening, where it closes within twelve months of the opening date, carries no annual fee.
- While the military rate cap is in force on the account, no annual fee is billed.
- Tiers priced at 0.00 USD for the annual fee never show an annual fee entry.
- No account is billed more than one annual fee in an account year, as the bank's records for the account and statement cycle show.

## Refund when the card is closed

Where the cardholder closes the account within the 30 calendar days that follow the posting of the annual fee, the fee is reversed in its entirety on the bank error ground. Once those 30 calendar days have run out, the fee is neither refunded nor prorated.

| Closure relative to the fee's posting | Outcome for the fee |
|---|---|
| Closed within the 30 calendar days after posting | reversed in full, bank error ground |
| Closed after those 30 calendar days | fee stands in full; no partial refund |

## Worked cases (hypothetical dates)

- An annual fee posts on 4 February and the cardholder closes the card on 16 February, 12 calendar days later: the fee comes back in full.
- The same fee, with the card closed on 20 March, more than 40 calendar days after posting: the fee stays, and no share of it is refunded for the unused part of the year.
- A card opened in June on a tier that forgoes the first-year fee: the June statement that falls within twelve months of opening bears no annual fee, and the June statement a year later bears the full fee.
